He also remembers you personally and small details about you, which means a lot especially when as a freshman in big lecture halls. I highly highly recommend even if you are worried about public speaking this class will help you so so much!

David is an excellent professor and he makes comms what it should be- a stress free gen ed course. He is very lenient about grading and gives good feedback for improvement. I thought I had performed poorly on one of the speeches, but he only took 1 point off. David also makes the class very applicable to the real world- I feel more confident in my ability to talk to others, both professionally and casually, and he really makes it a point to give you lessons that you can take outside the classroom. The workload is super chill and can be completed in under 30 minutes each week. David also really does a good job connecting with his students and would highly recommend taking his class as your communication credit.

GREAT PROFESSOR!! He is an excellent professor and gives great feedback. He genuinely wants to see you succeed, even outside of the classroom. I was really nervous about taking a public speaking class, but he made everything feel more comfortable. He's a great guy!

She is super nice great way to fill in a gened you can tell that she cares about her students and makes the work really easy. There are a bunch of small assignments and 4 main large assignments. She makes it possible to fail one major assignment and still pass but just the small assignments. The first and last assignment have a specific prompt but for the other two you are able to choose what to present about. Make sure to go to class she does take attendance and give in class work that will help your grade. She also gives one free skip for her class you just need to email her before hand. she is also very understanding about missing class as long as its excused.

Actually the goat. He is such a funny, nice guy who has the experience and actually cares and it shows, could listen to him speak for hours. Going into this class, thought INAG/COMM/This gen ed was going to be yet another gen ed waste of time and money but Ballenger actually makes it worth while where you feel and can see your public speaking improve. 10/10 would recommend.

Super nice and very chill. She did not grade harshly at all and really seemed to care about her students. Really accommodating and gave good advice if we were nervous about public speaking. We had to give four speeches and she gave good feedback and in my experience you got a hundred it you met most of the guidelines and were within the time frame the speech had to be (you could time yourself on your phone as you were speaking). If you have to take comm take it with her!

Super friendly and outgoing. Makes a true effort to connect with his students and make sure the material is understandable. I really hate public speaking in general but I felt like I learned a lot of valuable lessons in this class that really did help me feel more confident during presenting. Very fair grader and makes sure to outline exactly what he is looking for for speeches. Make sure to keep a close eye on Canvas for over the weekend assignments because he does off for lateness. Overall great professor.

Definitely one of the best classes to fill a GenEd requirement. Dr. Sefton has clear love and enthusiasm for the course and makes it a point help all of her students improve their communication skills. There are no exams or quizzes, and the major assessments are four speeches, each increasing by 25 points from the last and getting gradually longer. Dr. Sefton gives extremely helpful feedback and if most of the class misses points on the same thing, she won't deduct points for it. We work a lot with random partners throughout the semester, and while attendance isn't mandatory, we normally do a small 5-point assignment each class. All in all, definitely a great class to work on your public speaking and communication skills, and Dr. Sefton is honestly so amazing at her job.

Mr. B is great, he is super personable, funny, and remembers all his students, even remembers what they say they did for break. I hate public speaking but actually feel like I am so much better at it from this class. It is not too much work but you still learn something and you get to choose your speech topics which makes them easier because you can pick things you know about. he is clear with his expectations of your speeches, and the points that they are worth increase which is nice because you get better at it overtime. if you need a oral comms credit definitely take it with him!

he's a great guy! however, don't take this class if you like skipping! attendance is mandatory!!! also he does call on people randomly so you have to be comfortable with that. he is pretty lenient when it comes to grades and he is very clear with his expectations. i've had a better experience in INAG110 compared to most of my peers who took COMM107.

This professor was amazing. If you can get past the fact he may be insane, the class is extremely enjoyable for a comm class and super easy. The tests are open notes and super easy and he grades very lightly. Just be warned you need a suit, tie, dress pants, and dress shoes for the final speech of the class, so make sure you have them.

I absolutely hate public speaking and was not looking forward to completing the oral communication GenEd. However, this class has been amazing because Sam is one of the greatest professors. There is no such thing as a "boring" class with Sam. He makes every class period interesting with his never-ending enthusiasm. The class is also an incredibly easy A; it's basically impossible not to get an A. As long as you show up to class, participate, and complete your speeches, you will get an A. Don't go into this class expecting it to be normal. There is screaming, jokes, throwing chairs, and lots of laughter. Sam genuinely cares so much about his students and their learning. He is always going out of his way to provide support and help students out, inside and outside of class. He is one of the few teachers who doesn't do this job for money or for research but teaches to make an impact on students. And he does. Sam has grown my confidence in public speaking to new heights. I never thought I could speak without being nervous, but with Sam, I can. If you have the opportunity to take INAG110 with Sam, you 100% should. Sam is the goat.
Amazing professor, he's super sweet and inviting, and he makes INAG enjoyable and not too difficult. The class didn't feel like busy work, but I never felt overwhelmed by the content or speeches.

This class genuinely made me a better speaker and he's a really nice guy who is great at lecturing! The class has impromptu speeches that serve as a great way to practice. There are four main speeches you present with each one weighted more than the last. Basically, this means that as you improve, your entire grade will improve.
Dr. Gormong the GOAT. Super chill, super easy class, super caring about his students. Can't recommend this more.

Great professor. Genuinely cares about the students in class and is a very positive guy overall. Extremely chill class and as long as you show up and somewhat prepare for speeches (I literally just ran through it a few times the day of) you will do fine. Only points that would really get deducted is points off for being over/under time. Very chill guy and would 100% recommend if you need speech credit.

I LOVE PROFESSOR GORMONG. He is genuinely one of the nicest, most understanding professors I've ever had. The one thing about this class that I didn't like is that attendance is mandatory because there are weekly quizzes. But these quizzes are free Canvas quizzes that are unbelievably easy. The course has 4 speeches, and each one is not hard. Prof. Gormong grades very fairly, and it's hard to do bad with how well he teaches. If you have mental health issues or anything, he's super accommodating and understanding. PLEASE TAKE HIM FOR INAG, IT IS SO WORTH IT.
Take her!!! She's so fun and sweet and chill.
He the goat. Very kind and gives great feedback!
Amazing professor!!!! Cares about you, gives amazing feedback, and wants to see you do better. He genuinely made me so much better at public speaking and is a great person.

If you're looking to fulfill a gened with an easy A class, take this one. Professor Gormong is a bright person who always tries to keep the class interesting and interactive. There are 4 speeches you give in this class and most of them I just worked on for an hour or two the night before. The last one is an 8 minute speech but honestly it wasn't as scary as it sounds. This class has a very light workload. I didn't spend more than 10 minutes a week on it unless there was a big speech coming up. Professor Gormong is also a great person to talk to outside of class. He really loves and cares about his students and I had many great conversations with him outside of class. He also is very understanding if you need to miss class due to illness. I didn't even have to go through the hassle of acquiring doctor's notes when I missed class past my self excused absence. As long as you email him in time with a good reason, he's very understanding and just excuses you from any work missed. Highly recommend this class!
Very kind! Assignments all good and minimal busy work. Not stressful.

Very very rubric oriented. She will dock points for things that wouldn’t matter in the real world: I lost five points on a 75-point speech for saying “Thank You” at the end. Someone else said tunnel vision and I agree- you have to be careful about specific phrases like “I think” because it will count as persuasive/ opinionated language in an informative speech and you’ll lost points. 

Despite all that, it’s an easy class and there are enough completion assignments that your grade will be okay even if you make mistakes in the 4 speeches. 
I had an in-person class on Tuesdays and virtual on Thursdays- most in-person classes were people speaking or a short lecture. Thursdays were asynchronous work- you had 75 min to complete 2 written reflections and 1 video recording, and all 3 are completion grades out of 20 or 25 points. These assignments are only open during the class time, so be sure to set an alarm because she doesn’t accept any late work at all. Also, make sure to submit all your speech stuff when it’s due. Even if you already shared your PPT with her, if you don’t submit it to the Canvas assignment you’ll get a 0 on it and then she’ll be mean to you if you ask about it.

Amazing professor!!! It is very clear he cares about you and wants you to succeed. Compared to my friends that took COMM instead of INAG I feel he prepared me so much more than other professors. He gives amazing feedback and isn't a harsh grader. You don't spend much time at all doing work outside of class either. Highly recommend him if you're looking to take Communications, I improved so much over the semester.

Best professor I've had so far! Dr. Sefton truly made the class feel like a fun and welcoming environment. She tries very hard to remember all of her students names, and genuinely cares about how your day is going. Multiple times throughout the semester, she gave us a new partner to do in-class assignments with. These assignments are incredibly easy, and I honestly enjoyed getting to talk to new people.

There are a few recording assignments throughout the semester, but these too are very easy as long as you follow the rubric. There are a couple readings(chat GPT summaries) that she assigns before class, but you'll do fine even if you forget to read it. In terms of the main assignments (speeches), there are 4 throughout the year. Intro speech (1.5-2.5 minutes), informative speech (4-5 minutes), persuasive speech (5-6 minutes), and Professional Presentation (8-10 minutes). These are well distributed and I never practiced my speeches for more than 1.5 hours, total. 

Overall, she truly cares about your success as a speaker, and will give you great feedback. I will definitely use what I learned in class for any public speaking in the future. Before this class I was weary about public speaking, but I think this is genuinely one of the most important and beneficial classes I have taken so far. II definitely recommend taking Dr. Sefton!

Great professor, very chill grader (basically 100s on everything if you put in a bit of effort and follow the rubric), kind, and cares about you as a student and person. Helpful if you actually want to improve on your oral communication skills and even if not good person to take this class with. You have to go to class but honestly that is the bare minimum.
The class is pretty easy, and you should get an A as long as you show up.
Eric Dunning is an amazing teacher that lets u skip lectures if u feel like it. U just need to show up for class activties u can find on the syllabus.

He's a chill professor. Nothing crazy, no hard assignments, talks aren't that bad, gives pretty good feedback and is willing to help. I would recommend this course if you want a more laid back comms class.

If you are looking for an easy professor to get the comm gen ed out of the way take her. If you are looking to actually get better at public speaking she's not really the person for that in my opinion. Most of the assignments are for completion and they will be like little vlogs or watch this video and answer questions etc. She's very straightforward for what she's looking for in speeches like structure wise but that does limit you a little bit because you are adhering to HER definition of a good speech but the rubrics clearly tell you what that means. Just make sure you stay on top of the work because she won't expect late work and sometimes the speeches happen very close to each other. Don't forget your Pause 2 Reflects and turn in your outline/slide due before speeches and you will be just fine. I also thought she was a generally cool person to talk to after class and I loved how she always a gave little comments about everyone's topics after they spoke (not any critiques just something like "ikr food insecurity is such a problem or that's interesting i didn't know that"). Plus, she almost always lets you out early and considers the fact it's boring to listen to an hour worth of speeches.

Very easy class. Its easy to get an A if you follow the rubric for speeches. If you want an easy comm course I definitely recommend Amy Fisher, but I will say I'm coming out of the class with the same communication skills I had when I entered.

I loved this class and I loved her. The class was less than 20 people, which made the speeches super chill. The only thing is that she can be a little disorganized, but she has acknowledged this fault and is super understanding if she makes any sort of mistake. I definitely recommend taking this class in a semester where you know you will have a lot going on (i.e. first semester) because it is so unserious and fun.
Pretty chill class

BEST PROF!! Dr. Sefton makes each class fun, and she truly cares about each of her students. She clearly has extensive experience and is exceptionally good at teaching the class, knowing where people typically make mistakes and providing strategies to help us learn and remember the content.

Dr. Sefton also takes the time to learn and engage with her students. As a first-year student, she made this class a fun place to meet fellow students and even attended one of my music performances! After taking this class, she said she'd always be happy to support us in other ways (recommendation letters, reviewing grad school apps, etc.), and that was really sweet and stuck with me.

Overall, the class is pretty easy, and I definitely improved my public speaking skills. I've heard from friends about COMM107 and the other GenEd options, and this one seems to be the best if you need to get your requirement. Would absolutely recommend taking a class with Dr. Sefton!

Dr. Sefton is a really nice person and wants you to succeed in the class. However, she can be a bit of a harsh grader, so make sure you're following the rubric for the assignments. Overall, the class is easy and really boring. You have 4 different speeches, a handful of recorded videos you have to do, and a final reflection recording that replaces your final. Also, make sure you go to class since that makes up 5% of your grade. I ended up getting lazy at the end of the semester and stopped showing up

I took this course online. Professor Fisher was pretty laid-back and nice.

In my experience, it was really easy to get an A as long as you followed the instructions and didn't sound like a robot or read completely off a manuscript when doing your speeches. The grading was not harsh at all - the mean/median for all the speeches was above a 90, and she gave everyone a free 100% for the first introduction speech.

After the first week or two, she made all Monday/Wednesday classes optional for attendance, and Friday classes asynchronous. For the asynchronous work, it was slightly irritating since you only had the one-hour class time window to complete the assignments, and she did not accept any late work at all.

A heads-up for those taking her class in the future - she is only going to be teaching online and is planning on updating the course (I think one of the changes is a group project), so the class will probably look different from mine.

She was an amazing teacher. The class itself was easy enough if you put in some effort. There were 4 speeches which were not too bad, but stressed me out a little because I left them until the night before (do not do that). She also tried to make the class more fun through assignments like game days and the fairy tale mock trial, which I thought were pretty cool. She also gives extra credit (and a lot of it) so it was really easy to end with >100% in the class. Also, Mays-Williams was really nice and put in the effort to learn our names and talk to us. Overall, super chill class if you don't procrastinate the speeches.

Professor Gormong is extremely nice. I know communications is a relatively easy class, and he grades very chill. If you do an assignment wrong, you can redo it until you get a 100 percent. He also grades major speeches relatively easy. The only thing I'd say is, he gives more work than other comms professors. There are weekly quizzes and practice speeches(still easy though but just more work). And you have weekly assignments. Take him if you want the A, but be prepared to put in more work, it's just busy work though. Also, attendance IS mandatory, or you get a 0 on the assignments from that day.

like all of the other reviews say, sam is such an energetic and caring professor! attending the class was mandatory, but it never felt boring or a chore despite that (most classes are listening to other peoples' speeches, the remaining ones were lecture days). in terms of workload, the class is also very laid back - we had two "communication activities" at the beginning of the semester (graded on completion), a couple multiple-choice quizzes that we did after each lecture, two "midterms" (one was just an essay, and the second one was an open-note quiz and essay), one "final" (an open-note quiz and essay), and three speeches (weighted 75%, 100%, and 125% each - your materials for the speech were due a class period before you presented, and a reflection essay was due the class period after you presented). my only complaint about his class is that his penalty for going over on speeches felt a bit harsh - i went over time on the first speech, and was deducted an entire letter grade on the speech because of that. that deduction was the only reason why i didn't get an a+ in the class despite getting a's on my other speeches, which irritated me a bit but admittedly does not matter that much

I would like to preface this by saying that I despise public speaking, and therefore absolutely abhorred this class; I would get stomachaches from anxiety every day before I left my dorm to go to this class. That being said, Mr. B is a great professor. My deep hatred of this class had nothing to do with him--if anything, he made the class better overall; I am just someone who struggles with anxiety, and a deep fear of public speaking. 

This class emphasizes speech writing, which I had never really done before, so it was a helpful instruction in a new area for me. There are 4 main speeches, each one getting longer and adding more layers onto what you're required to present, and there are also impromptu speaking assignments on most days; but as the course goes on, you definitely feel prepared for each speech that comes your way. Mr. B is a very fair and forgiving grader--as long as you clearly put in the effort for writing and rehearsing your speeches, you're very likely to get an A. He also gives fantastic feedback, especially if you utilize office hours. I'd recommend going to office hours at least once per major speech and running your speech by him before you're due to present; a lot of anxiety is saved knowing if you're on the right track or not and what you need to do to make your speech even better, which in turn improves your confidence once you do need to present. He very clearly cares about his students and their success, and he fosters a pretty good environment in class. You definitely see your public speaking skills improve. 

Did I enjoy this class? Absolutely not. But I was never going to, regardless of who I took it with. I knew I wouldn't magically enjoy this class if I had a good instructor. But the bottom line is that Mr. B is a great teacher to take comm107/inag110 with. Perhaps there's a professor out there who doesn't have their students speak as much, but if you're looking to actually get better at speaking and writing speeches, and want to do so with a professor who you know is committed to making sure his students do the best they possibly can, he's the guy to take.

He’s a really nice guy overall! He is a bit strict on grading. A lot of other teachers gave all their students a 100 on their speeches, but he was kind of nit-picky with taking off points for small things, though never anything enough to tank your grade. He is really nice overall, though, and the workload is not too bad at all. Weekly quizzes, but they’re really simple. Overall, you should take him, but I heard Mays-Williams is a bit better for an easier A (even though his class is also an easy A).

Great INAG teacher, his voice is very reporter like, he has small quizzes that are open note and essentially grade boosters, and grades you fairly on the speeches as long as you simply take the feedback from the last speech and implement it in your next.

She is a really nice teacher for the most part. Make sure you come to class and on time. You can lose participation points if you're even just 2 minutes late. She is a nice grader on speeches so it shouldn't be too hard to do well in the class.

I think this professor really embodies the values of UMD. I was not at all excited to do any public speaking, but she made this class as fun as she could. She makes great connections with students, is super understanding about life, and is always supportive and approachable. She even offers extra credit, so really just read the rubrics and put in any effort at all. She has super reasonable expectations. Also is very in touch with pop culture, which can be reflected in her speech examples.

always so kind and goes out of his way to make a welcoming environment for everyone. as someone who struggles with anxiety over public speaking he made the speeches very manageable, he grades very leniently and genuinely just wants to see you improve over the semester at public speaking and communication. he does give weekly practice speeches but those are basically just participation grades and are just so that you can improve your speaking skills. would absolutely recommend
Great guy and teacher but honestly grades too harshly, especially for a gened comms class. I would recommend comm107 instead.
She was engaging and made it to learn about each student. I also feel like I actually learned something about oral communication. Nice lady

I definitely would recommend taking a course with him. He is so genuinely nice and welcoming, he deeply cares for his students' wellbeing, he is an insanely fast grader, and he gives good feedback. Taking his class was so worth it. I have terrible social anxiety, but this environment made speaking so much easier.

Definitely enjoyed this class more than I thought I would, but the content is obviously pretty intuitive. It is good public speaking practice, and I thought Dr. Sefton worked hard to make sure we were learning something new every class. She does grade a little harshly on speeches in my opinion, but that's literally the "midterms" of the class so I can't say I blame her. She's a good professor though, and I totally recommend to anyone who needs their oral communications credit.

honestly, no complaints. she made all the assignments very clear and was super nice about any questions. she tried her hardest to get to know each student, and she is an easy grader. showing up and not being on your phone is important (she gives your section extra credit if you guys are phone-less for the semester). everything for the class is super straightforward--completely recommend her.
This class is the best and Sam is the goat.  Take him!

Incredible professor. The other reviews are right, he is a very unusual professor, and he gives the "fun uncle" vibe more than a professor vibe. He is hilarious, and he makes edgy jokes which are super funny if you are that type of person. He also brings a level of energy in the class that I have never seen before. He is super engaging but also really caring. This was the only class that I looked forward to going to every single time. I took this class a while back, and I have recommended him to every single friend of mine. The class is definitely not for everyone, but if you take it, you'll definitely have stories to tell for the rest of college (in a good way). I miss his classes, and him as a professor. The chair throwing, water spilling, the human centipede jokes, and everything else turned into memories that I miss. Any rating except a 5/5 is too low for him. Guys, trust me, just take him!
Very specific about grading, kind of harsh for a gen ed. Nice guy but take the class online!

I'm going to have to slander the goat here, so I'm sorry Mr. B in advance.

This guy actually teaches comms. And I have to say, I've learned a lot for being a comms class. But, he's a bit of a harsh grader for a class every student on campus takes. I truly believe that he does this so we actually learn how to give speeches.

Otherwise, he's actually the best comms teacher on campus. Don't skip out on this guy.

(mandatory attendance; light-medium homework)

name: INAG110
title: Oral Communication
description: Credit only granted for: COMM107, COMM200, INAG110, JOUR130, THET285. A study of how perception, self-concept, and verbal and nonverbal communications affect the communication process as it emerges in the workplace. The course provides skill training in speech writing, public speaking, group communication, interpersonal communication, listening, and responding.
